01

Executive summary

eBay Fresh is a speculative concept video: an explainer for a grocery-delivery service imagined as an extension of eBay's brand, not an existing eBay product.

I built this as a practical exercise in converting a multifaceted, slightly abstract business idea (fresh produce sourcing, local farming support, sustainable delivery) into an explainer video a general audience could follow in under a minute. It's a self-initiated design exercise, not commissioned or official eBay work, and I want that distinction clear from the outset.

02

Background

This project sat alongside two other motion graphics pieces built during the same module, and the certifications behind all three were specific and deliberate: After Effects CC 2022 and 2023 Essential Training, Motion Graphic Design (Animation and Composition modules), and Cinema 4D S22 Essential Training for Motion Graphics. eBay Fresh was where the character rigging and 2D/3D compositing skills from that training got their first real workout.

03

The brief

Present a speculative eBay grocery-delivery service to a general audience, showcasing its advantages (local farming support, fresh produce, sustainable delivery) while inspiring viewers to make more sustainable shopping choices.

04

Objectives

  • Educate and engage: inform viewers about the service's selling points through engaging visuals and narration.
  • Drive action and adoption: motivate viewers to imagine trying the service, closing on a call to action toward a website and app.
  • Promote sustainability and local farming: foreground the service's role in supporting sustainable agriculture and local farming communities.
  • Build brand image: position the concept as forward-thinking, eco-friendly and creative, more community project than pure commerce.
  • Community engagement: invite viewers to see themselves as part of a community making sustainable choices.
05

Brand system

I built a full type and colour system rather than borrowing eBay's existing one wholesale. Typography runs across three families: Roboto across its full weight range for body and functional text, Gilroy in Heavy and Extra Bold for high-impact moments, and Univers (including its condensed cuts) for anything needing a tighter, more technical feel.

The colour direction kept eBay's actual brand colours (vivid red, bright blue, sunny yellow, lush green) as the anchor, specifically so the concept still read as recognisably part of the eBay family rather than an unrelated fictional brand. Around that anchor I built a much larger secondary palette of produce-inspired tones: rustic copper, vibrant tomato, mint leaf, forest pine, sunflower yellow, among dozens of others, giving the fresh-produce visuals somewhere to live tonally without ever fighting the core brand colours for attention.

06

Script

The script runs as four scenes building from a global framing device down to the specific product experience:

Scene 1
A vibrant Earth spins slowly in space; industrial smoke recedes on one side as green growth spreads across the other.
"Our planet is a masterpiece of life, a canvas of biodiversity and wonder. But it faces challenges that require innovative solutions and sustainable choices."
Scene 2
A woman opens her laptop; the screen opens into a virtual shopping world as the eBay Fresh logo and a shelf of produce appear.
"Welcome to a whole new shopping experience! Introducing eBay Fresh, your one-stop online grocery market, where freshness meets convenience."
Scene 3
A user browses the "Fresh" category, selects items, and completes a purchase.
"With just a few clicks, explore a wide variety of fresh produce, handpicked from local farms and trusted suppliers. It's shopping made simple, fast, and hassle-free."
Scene 4
A farmer harvests vegetables; a freshness-certification badge stamps onto the screen.
"Each product is carefully selected, ensuring it meets our high standards for freshness and quality. Plus, with eBay's Buyer Protection, your satisfaction is guaranteed."
07

Storyboard

The storyboard maps the journey of produce from farm to table through the service, and doubles as the point where I decided the video needed two distinct visual registers rather than one: flat 2D illustration for the human, browsing-and-buying moments, shifting toward more dimensional treatment for the farm and delivery sequences.

08

Production pipeline: rigging & assembly

The background started as a solid layer with a Fractal Noise effect in After Effects, tuned for a soft, organic texture rather than a flat colour field. Character and prop assets (laptop, desk, papers, the figure herself) were imported as separate vector layers specifically so each could be animated independently, with keyframed arm movement driving the typing action.

The globe used the CC Sphere effect to wrap a flat map onto a 3D-reading sphere, animated to rotate, with Glow layered on top for visual interest and a fractal-noise matte doing double duty as a transition device. The composition at this stage contained several shape layers and text elements indicating the layout of a webpage: the skeleton the rest of the animation would build on.

09

Production pipeline: animation & composition

A full set of vegetable illustrations went in as reusable assets, and the dropdown menu animation ("Fresh," "Vegetables," "Fruits") was built layer by layer to feel like a real interface rather than a mockup. A Corner Pin effect handled the laptop-screen perspective as the logo and interface changed on-screen, and the shopping cart icon with its "2" notification badge was purpose-built rather than a stock asset. The farmer character, offering a thumbs-up with a basket of produce, closes the loop back to the sourcing story from Scene 4.

10

Production pipeline: 3D, texturing & lighting

This is where Cinema 4D came in properly: a sphere surrounded by human figures, modelled to suggest connection and global reach, became the centrepiece for the closing brand moment. The eBay logo was integrated into that 3D scene with its own material pass, and the human figures were textured and coloured individually so the arrangement read as a deliberate, dynamic bond around the central globe rather than a repeated clone.

Bringing the 3D globe-and-figures render back into After Effects to composite with the 2D logo work (plus a CC Image Wipe on the sustainability icon and a Bulge effect drawing focus to the final "ebay.com/fresh" call to action) was the specific challenge of marrying the two halves of the pipeline into one consistent look.

11

Text animation

Typography carried a lot of the thematic weight on its own: "BIODIVERSITY" and "WONDER" flanking the spinning globe in the opening, "INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS" and "SUSTAINABLE CHOICES" wrapping a luminous globe in the sustainability beat, and a late change to how "SUSTAINABLE PLANET" moved through the frame specifically to add a stronger sense of depth around the planet rather than sitting flat against it. The farmer scene went through its own revision pass: an abstracted visual treatment of the plucking motion, plus motion added to "FRESHNESS & QUALITY" so the key selling point didn't just sit static on screen.

12

Sound design

The voiceover was generated using veed.io's AI voice tool, chosen specifically for natural-sounding speech synthesis and a voice matching the brand's intended character: friendly, informative, trustworthy. The script was written to be spoken clearly at a consistent pace before it went anywhere near the tool.

Music came from Uppbeat, a royalty-free track called "Seize the Day" by Andrey Rossi, chosen for an upbeat, modern feel that mirrors the motion graphics' own pacing. Final mixing happened in Adobe Audition: balancing voiceover against music so narration always sat clearly on top, EQ to keep the music out of the voice's frequency range, compression to hold a consistent volume across quiet and loud passages, timing adjustments to align audio cues with on-screen action, subtle UI sound effects on interface moments, and a final master pass for consistency across playback environments.

13

Reflection

The real skill this project tested was the seam between 2D and 3D work: the Cinema 4D globe composited back into a flat interface animation, without either half looking like it belonged to a different piece. Getting that seam invisible, rather than getting either half individually polished, was the actual challenge.

Working against eBay's real brand colours rather than inventing a fictional palette from scratch was a deliberate constraint, and one I'd defend: it's what keeps a speculative concept honest about being a design exercise rather than pretending to be an unrelated original brand.

14

Lessons learned

Build the 3D asset and its texturing and lighting as a genuinely finished piece before worrying about how it'll composite into the 2D work around it. Every time I tried to shortcut that on this project, rushing a texture pass because I knew After Effects would be doing more work on top of it later, the seam between the two showed.

15

Skills demonstrated

Concept & script development Storyboarding 2D character rigging 3D modelling & lighting 2D/3D compositing Kinetic typography AI voice generation Sound mixing (Adobe Audition)
16

Interview story

Situation

My motion graphics module required a brand explainer video demonstrating both 2D character animation and 3D integration within a single piece.

Task

Build a speculative grocery-delivery concept for an existing brand, convincing enough to read as a real product video in under a minute, without access to that brand's actual internal design resources.

Action

I built a full brand and colour system anchored in eBay's real identity, wrote a four-scene script moving from a global framing device to the specific product experience, and rigged and animated the human character and interface elements in After Effects before building a Cinema 4D globe sequence and compositing the two together.

Result

A complete, professionally paced explainer video with a coherent 2D-to-3D visual language throughout, and a genuine understanding of how to keep a speculative concept honest to its real-world reference rather than inventing an unrelated aesthetic.
